column1: # Baseline runs -- what each module looked like BEFORE any formal-driven fix,
# measured with TODAY's harness.
# Method -- four lines, nothing to remember:
#   W=$(mktemp -d) && git worktree add $W --detach 61f0575 && cd $W
#   git checkout f667f74 -- formal/          # today's harness onto the old RTL
#   git cherry-pick --no-commit <enabling...>   # in the order this table lists
#   formal/run.sh <config>                   # BRAM: baseline/<config>
# Cherry-pick ONLY the named commits, in order. Never hand-edit: an assembled state
# that never existed is how F-26's investigation went wrong.
# THE BRAM CONFIGS LIVE IN A SUBFOLDER. formal/{bind,tcl}/baseline/ holds
# black-box-only variants, invoked as `formal/run.sh baseline/bram_tree_baseline`.
# run.sh needs no change: it builds formal/tcl/${m}.tcl, and its outdir is mkdir -p,
# so artifacts land in formal/jgproject/baseline/<config>/, away from the main suite.
# The subfolder is also why `run.sh --all` still sees exactly 13 configs -- its glob
# is formal/tcl/*.tcl and is NOT recursive. Keeping variant families in a subfolder
# is what stops them contaminating the 13/13 number HANDOFF quotes.
# NOTE ON LABELLING: a red row is a SHORTCOMING, not necessarily a defect. Some are
# contract questions (F-1/CH-4) where the disposition was containment, not repair.
# The manifest records what the run showed and the disposition separately.
# BASELINE = 61f0575 (2026-08-19), the last commit before the first formal-driven
# RTL fix (52ae5a9). Every module already carries the uniform six-port interface.
# HONESTY CAVEAT, to be repeated in the write-up: this is NOT "the design as
# originally written". At 2c8a4d6 the modules exposed o_full/o_empty -- different
# signals, different paths. The uniform interface arrived at e7c20ad, which is the
# formal effort's OWN work. The claim this table supports is "the design as it
# stood when verification began, once a common interface existed".
# enabling: comma-separated commits, IN CHERRY-PICK ORDER. "-" means none.
# whitebox: whether the aux addenda can bind at baseline at all. BLACK-BOX ONLY IS
#   A DELIBERATE SCOPE DECISION for this table, not a shortfall -- the white-box
#   results belong to the full findings write-up. Where the aux happens to bind
#   (the register family) it is included because it costs nothing; where it cannot
#   (the BRAM modules, whose aux watches signals the fixes created) the row simply
#   says so. Do not read a clean black-box row as "the module was sound": the
#   sweep measured F-32 as caught by exactly one property, and it is white-box.
# ENABLING COMMITS come in three kinds, and the write-up should distinguish them:
#   infrastructure  - fa7b2c9, parameterisation so the proof can be sized
#   measurability   - 52ae5a9 (F-6, elaboration), 26adf6d/bbc3ef2 (F-21, the harness
#                     refuses a multiply-driven design) -- each is ITSELF a finding
#   unblocking      - 406c076 (F-28). A finding fixed to make OTHER findings visible.
#                     A row carrying this is no longer "the baseline"; it is the
#                     baseline after the blocking defect was cleared. Label it.
# COLUMN POSITIONS ARE ALIGNED WITH mutations/SWEEP.tsv ON PURPOSE: field 1 is the
# CLI key, field 5 is the ref --replay rebuilds at, field 7 is the machine-checked
# expectation, field 8 is prose. That alignment is what lets regress.sh share its
# dispatch, control runs, drift warning and verdict parsing across both manifests
# instead of growing a second slightly-different copy of them (see F-13).
# ref (field 5) MEANS SOMETHING DIFFERENT PER MANIFEST, and this is the one place
# the two modes genuinely diverge:
#   SWEEP    the commit the worktree is CHECKED OUT at   (the design moved)
#   BASELINE the commit formal/ is OVERLAID from         (the instrument moved)
# In baseline mode the checkout is ALWAYS pinned to the baseline commit in field 3.
# If it ever follows field 5 instead, the row silently measures TODAY's RTL while
# claiming to measure the pre-verification design -- it runs, it looks plausible,
# and it is the F-26 assembled-configuration error wearing a new coat.
# expect vocabulary (same as SWEEP, plus one extension):
#   clean                    0 cex and 0 unreachable covers; a verdict block MUST exist
#   cex:a,b,c                ALL named leaves must fire -- not "at least one"
#   cover-unreachable:<n>    vacuity, pinned to a count
# WHY cex TAKES A LIST HERE. A baseline row's whole value is the BREADTH of what
# the harness still sees. Pinning one leaf would let systolic_array quietly drop
# from five counterexamples to one and still report CAUGHT, which is precisely the
# weakened-spec case this table exists to detect.
#row
